trickyParts: nats-server 2.10.29 and 2.12.15 lose a push consumer's message whose first delivery is in the server's send queue when the deliver subject's last subscriber goes (didNotDeliver wraps the redelivery count; hasMaxDeliveries removes it at the ack wait). A graceful stop therefore keeps its subscription until the next holder is receiving.
A graceful release always carries unsettled=true: messages handed back with a 2 s NAK delay must not be overtaken by newer ones the next holder receives first, so it settles (about 2 s).
deviations: The linger ends after 1 s when no other pod takes the released record (not the 3 s cap): a sole pod gains nothing by lingering and the 3 s per stop pushed the untagged suite past go's 10-minute default. Residual: the last pod of a machine stopping can still meet the nats-server loss above for a message in flight at that instant; no client-side fix exists without another subscriber.
